answer.why: As an insider, 'Confirmed & Substantive' made me laugh straight away because it is the exact phrase from the HR letter after probation or promotion, and a game that knows that detail probably gets the rest right. 'Minister Salary' sounds like a clickbait jab at the ministerial pay debate, and I have heard that joke at every kopitiam since 2011. I would still be curious about it, but I would assume it is a cheap shot, so the first name wins.
answer.expect_minister_salary: A satirical or cynical game that is all about the pay benchmark, with a smug punchline about earning millions. I would expect a meme-level take on the salary controversy, probably a shallow clicker where you chase money and the details of the service are wrong or ignored. It would be catchy and shareable, but I would not expect it to understand how people actually move through the grades.
answer.expect_confirmed_substantive: A dry, insider-flavoured career sim that shows real knowledge of the service: probation, confirmation in appointment, acting versus substantive posts, appraisals and the slow grind up the ladder. I would expect humour from the bureaucratic wording, the quiet politics and a lot of small trade-offs rather than a big money chase. The name is a bit clunky and might put off outsiders, but it feels written by someone who has actually sat in the meetings.

Lost the Ward

Forty-eight point two percent. You shook every hand in that ward and it was not enough, and it was never going to be about you anyway.

YOUR CEILING: When you joined, your file put no ceiling on you inside the service. Most people's files do.

THE YEAR IT CHANGED: At 38, in The Officer You Nominated, you chose "Let her decide without hearing from you." It raised your ceiling to Deputy Prime Minister.

LEGACY: People you trained quote you in rooms you will never enter. Two of them say you are the reason they stayed.
